findings.element: .b-edit inside .b-stick at every two-column width (render-b.js openEditor/keepInBand; b.css @media (min-width:1024px) .b-stick{position:sticky})
findings.problem: Driven, not read. Opening the editor at 1440x960, 1280x900, 1152x800 and 1024x768 puts the panel at top 597 and bottom 1156 (height 559px, of which 88px is the reserved undo band) and nothing scrolls: openEditor() ends on node.focus({preventScroll:true}), and keepInBand() returns at its first line unless getComputedStyle(panel).position === 'fixed', which it never is at >=1024. Measured: Done lands at y=1036 and Delete at y=1100 against viewports of 960, 900, 800 and 768 — the primary confirm and the one destructive control are off screen the moment the panel appears, at every desk width, and the panel has max-height:none/overflow:visible there so nothing hints at more below. Tabbing then makes it worse, because the panel is pinned inside .b-stick while the browser scrolls the document to reveal the next stop: at 1440 the step from 'Move a week later' to 'Shown' scrolls the plan column 525px under a stationary editor; at 1152 the traversal jumps 449px, then 465px, and the moment being edited leaves the screen entirely at 'Done' (rowTop -282); at 1024 it leaves at 'Shown' (rowTop -153) and never returns; at 1280x900 Delete is not on screen at any point in the traversal up to and including Done. The behaviour gate cannot see any of this: 'the row being edited is on screen when it opens' and 'the move is on screen where it happens' (interaction-check.mjs:989, 993) run only at 390 and 768, the two widths where the panel IS fixed and keepInBand does run.
findings.fix: Two edits. (1) In render-b.js keepInBand(), replace the early return with a static-panel branch: when position is not 'fixed', read box = panel.getBoundingClientRect() and, if box.bottom > window.innerHeight, window.scrollBy(0, Math.round(Math.min(box.bottom - window.innerHeight + 16, box.top - 16))); call keepInBand(root, item) at the end of openEditor() after node.focus(). (2) In b.css, inside @media (min-width:1024px), add `[data-editor-open] .b-stick { position: static; }` so the horizon column releases its pin while the editor is open and the panel, the row it edits and the plan all scroll as one body instead of the plan sliding out from under a fixed editor. Then extend interaction-check.mjs:978 to run the 'on screen when it opens' / 'on screen where it happens' loop at 1024, 1152, 1280 and 1440, and add an assertion that the panel's Done and Delete are both inside the viewport on open.

findings.element: --b-sheet, written once in render-b.js openEditor(); b.css:40 .b-field[data-editor-open]{padding-bottom:var(--b-sheet,var(--gap-block))} and @media (max-width:1023px) scroll-padding-bottom
findings.problem: openEditor() writes --b-sheet only once, and only `if (getComputedStyle(node).position === 'fixed')`. Nothing recomputes it afterwards: render-core.js binds resize to settle() alone, and __TLD.b.settle only re-places the measures. So a window that is narrowed while the editor is open — a laptop window dragged in, a tablet rotated, a split view — docks the sheet to the bottom edge with no band reserved for it. Measured: open at 1440x960, resize to 768x1024 and the panel flips to position:fixed with --b-sheet still unset, so .b-field falls back to var(--gap-block) = 28px of padding-bottom and scroll-padding-bottom falls back to 30px. The document is 2499px against the 3054px it measures when the same editor is opened natively at 768 — 555px of reserved layout simply missing. Scroll to the true bottom and two row Edit controls sit under the sheet with no scroll left to free them (natively opened at 768 the same test strands zero); at 390 after the same resize, one. This is the paid-for class 'floating objects erase what is under them' returning through the one path the gate does not walk: 'the sheet reserves its own band @ 390/768' (interaction-check.mjs:1001) is only ever run on a page that was LOADED at that width, never on one resized into it.
findings.fix: In render-b.js, replace the one-shot write in openEditor() with a reserve(root) helper and call it from both openEditor() and __TLD.b.settle (which render-core.js already runs on every resize and on fonts.ready): `function reserve(root){ var p = root && root.querySelector('.b-edit'); if(!p) return; if (getComputedStyle(p).position === 'fixed') root.style.setProperty('--b-sheet', (p.offsetHeight + 24) + 'px'); else root.style.removeProperty('--b-sheet'); }` — in settle, resolve root as document.querySelector('.b-field[data-editor-open]'). Then add an assertion to interaction-check.mjs that opens owner-editing at 1440, calls page.setViewportSize({width:768,height:1024}), scrolls to the bottom and requires zero stranded .b-grab and field padding-bottom >= panel.offsetHeight, and the same test in the 390 direction.

findings.element: 701–1023px: b.css @media (min-width:701px) [data-medium="full"] raises, against @media (min-width:1024px) [data-medium="full"] .b-two, and ownerScale() in render-b.js
findings.problem: The two-column composition now begins at 1024, but the desk GEOMETRY still begins at 701 — the count lane goes to 124px, titles to 24px, the count to 148px, and ownerScale() returns 18px/day at exactly 701 — so the band 701–1023 gets the desk measure inside a single column. Measured across 701, 768, 834, 900 and 1023: the first moment sits at y=967 (937 at 900 and 1023), there are 282px of empty rail above the first tick, and the document is 2527px against 2130px at 1024 — 397px taller for the same plan. At 1023x800 that means an owner opening their own plan sees a counter, a date, a today rule, a gap note and an empty rail, and not one moment: y=937 against an 800px fold, and 219px of dead field to the right of every row. Those are the same numbers the round-7 note records as the defect that moving the boundary fixed ('the first moment at y=941, below an 800px fold ... 456px of empty field beside each row'). The boundary moved; the class stayed one pixel below it, on iPad portrait (768/834), on a Surface split view and on any browser window that is not maximised. The gate's own two-column assertions (interaction-check.mjs:2481–2485, 'the owner sees a moment without scrolling') run only at widths >= 1024, so this band is graded by nothing at all.
findings.fix: Bind the geometry to the same number as the composition. In b.css, move the `[data-medium="full"]` half of the desk raise block (lines 1256–1275: .b-num, .b-when, .b-measure, .b-measureHead, .b-rail, .b-item, .b-origin, .b-away, .b-tick, .b-title, .b-empty, .b-emptyTitle, .b-ended, .b-dayWrap) out of @media (min-width:701px) and into the existing @media (min-width:1024px) block, leaving the `[data-medium="sheet"]` selectors where they are so the 794px A4 sheet keeps its composition. In render-b.js ownerScale(), change `window.innerWidth >= 701` to `window.innerWidth >= 1024`. The 701–1023 band then renders the phone composition it is actually shaped like: the first moment returns to roughly y=790, inside the fold at 800 and comfortably inside it at 1024. Add the 768 and 1023 widths to the 'owner sees a moment without scrolling' loop.

findings.problem: The stalled load sets role="status" on the <section class="b-field">. Two consequences, both confirmed in the tree. First, the region landmark is destroyed: every other state exposes section[aria-label="The plan for Mara & Finn"] as a region, and on this one — the only screen where the audience meets failure — it is a status object instead. Second, and worse, the code contradicts its own comment eight lines below it, which says in as many words that this must not happen: 'A live region of its own. The .b-field cannot serve as one: it contains the button being pressed, so announcing through it re-reads the whole screen back at the person who pressed it.' The field does contain the Try again button, and role=status is aria-atomic by default, so every write inside it — says.textContent swapping to 'Bringing in what is ahead.' and back to the stalled sentence, note.style.display toggling, the aria-busy flip — re-reads the entire 137-character screen on top of the purpose-built .b-live region that was added precisely to avoid it. The measured gate never sees it either: interaction-check.mjs's accessibility-spine loop (line 258) visits phone, desk, print, owner-flight and day only, so neither 'the plan is a region' nor 'exactly one h1' has ever been run against loading-slow, publish, owner-empty, ended, loading, owner-editing or owner-undone — and publish, checked by hand, is the one real screen of the thirteen with zero h1, its 38/48px headline standing as an <h2> with nothing above it.
findings.fix: Delete the line `field.setAttribute("role", "status");` from states["loading-slow"] in render-b.js. aria-busy on the field already marks the wait and the .b-live paragraph added ten lines below is the announcer, so nothing is lost and the region comes back. Then extend the state list at interaction-check.mjs:258 to ["phone","desk","print","owner-flight","day","publish","owner-empty","loading","loading-slow","owner-editing"] and add `ok('the field is not itself a live region · ' + state, !document.querySelector('.b-field[role="status"]'))`. Publish will fail the h1 assertion when it is added: promote `h("h2.b-pressTitle", …)` to `h("h1.b-pressTitle", …)` in states.publish, which is what the screen already looks like.

findings.element: b.css:1236 `.b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body); }` against b.css:1263 `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-away { … font-size: var(--size-lead); }`
findings.problem: A dead rule on the keepsake. Both selectors are specificity (0,2,0); the media-query one is later in source and a media query adds no specificity, so `.b-print .b-away` loses at every width where the A4 sheet is actually composed. Measured on the print state: at 1440 and at 794 (A4 at 96dpi) the day-count column renders at 17px; only below 701 — a width at which nobody composes an A4 sheet — does it render at the 15px the rule asks for. The consequence is the class the library already charged for once: on the printed sheet the machine's figure and the person's words are now byte-identical in size and weight — .b-away at 17px/400 Geist Mono beside .b-title at 17px/400 Geist. The twin of this rule was noticed and patched: `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-print .b-title` is re-declared inside the media query at b.css:1276 and works. One of the pair got the fix and the other did not.
findings.fix: In b.css, delete line 1236 `.b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body); }` and add `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body); }` immediately after the existing `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-print .b-title` rule at line 1276, inside the same @media (min-width:701px) block. Add an assertion to the print section of interaction-check.mjs requiring getComputedStyle('.b-print .b-away').fontSize to be strictly smaller than getComputedStyle('.b-print .b-title').fontSize on the sheet.

biggestWin: The primary gesture holds up under driving, which is rare. setAway() is genuinely the only writer of a moment's distance, and everything downstream — the count in the gutter, the date line, the row's accessible name, the stepper readout, the WHEN field (guarded on focus, so a stepper press cannot lose to a half-typed value and a half-typed value is never yanked out from under the typist), the ceiling sentence, the disabled state of the four steppers and the horizon's gap sentence — is recomputed from that one ISO date in the same frame. I moved a moment twenty times, typed a date, renamed it, hid it, deleted it and undid every one of those, and at no point did the surface, the record and the accessibility tree disagree about what the plan said; the reversibility bar is one node that travels to the panel where the change is made, every entry carries its own closure and its own scroll position, and the undo of a move returns focus to the exact stepper that made it. That, plus the measure itself — position as real elapsed time at a declared pixels-per-day, the tick on the true pixel while the count travels with the words it names — is work at the Linear bar. What stands between it and 9.5 is not the idea and not the craft of the parts: it is the composition of the owner's editor at desk width, where a 559px panel opens into a sticky rail with its confirm and its delete below the fold and the plan then scrolls out from under it, and the 701–1023 band, which still carries the desk measure inside one column and so reproduces, at 1023x800, the exact screen round 7 recorded as fixed. Both are a build of a day or two each, not a redesign; the other three are polish.
